name: ZITLAS Sattu Power Shot
description: A 2-minute Bihar-inspired no-cook drink-meal made by whisking roasted gram flour into water with lemon and spices — built for a hostel room with zero cooking equipment.
instructions: Add sattu to a glass or bottle.
Pour in water and whisk hard with a spoon or fork until no lumps remain.
Stir in lemon juice, roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Drink immediately — sattu settles if left standing.
why_it_works: High protein with zero cooking
Works with just a bottle and spoon
Very low cost

name: ZITLAS Moong Cheela Paneer Roll
description: A savoury moong dal crepe rolled around a lightly spiced paneer-spinach filling — a complete protein breakfast eaten like a wrap.
ingredients: Moong dal (soaked, ground to batter) — 50 g
instructions: Grind soaked moong dal with ginger-chilli paste and a little water into a smooth, pourable batter.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a thin crepe. Cook 2 minutes until set.
Meanwhile, saute onion in oil with cumin seeds, then add paneer and spinach; cook 3-4 minutes.
Place the filling along one edge of the cheela and roll it up tightly.
Slice in half and serve warm.
why_it_works: Two complementary protein sources in one wrap
Naturally gluten-free
Portable once rolled

name: ZITLAS Leftover Rice Protein Poha
description: Turns yesterday's plain cooked rice into a soft, savoury breakfast by pan-tossing it poha-style with peanuts, moong sprouts and turmeric — no fresh grain needed.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil in a kadai, add mustard seeds and let them splutter, then add curry leaves and peanuts, roast lightly.
Add onion and saute until translucent.
Add moong sprouts and cook 2-3 minutes.
Add cold leftover rice and turmeric, breaking up any clumps, and toss on medium heat for 3-4 minutes until heated through.
Serve hot with a squeeze of lemon.
why_it_works: Prevents food waste from last night's rice
Sprouts add fresh crunch and protein
Ready in under 15 minutes

name: ZITLAS Egg Bhurji Paratha Roll
description: Spiced scrambled egg wrapped inside a whole wheat paratha, cut into a lunchbox-ready roll for the commute to office or college.
instructions: Knead the atta into a firm dough with water and roll out into a roti; roast on a dry tawa until lightly done.
In the same tawa, heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft.
Beat the egg and pour in, scramble with turmeric and chilli powder until fully cooked.
Spread the bhurji along the roti and roll it up tightly.
Wrap in foil or paper for carrying.
why_it_works: Complete protein wrapped for easy carrying
Uses one pan for both roti and filling
Good pre-commute breakfast

name: ZITLAS Overnight Chia Peanut Jar
description: Chia seeds and oats soaked overnight in milk with peanut butter and banana — no cooking required, ready to grab straight from the fridge.
instructions: Combine chia seeds, oats and milk in a jar, stir well to prevent clumping.
Add peanut butter and mix through.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight (minimum 6 hours).
Top with sliced banana just before eating.
why_it_works: Zero morning cooking time
High fiber from chia and oats
Can be prepped for 3-4 days at once

name: ZITLAS Kettle Oats with Roasted Chana
description: Rolled oats cooked using only boiling water from an electric kettle, finished with roasted chana and milk powder for crunch and protein — built for hostel rooms with no stove.
instructions: Boil water in the electric kettle.
Add oats and milk powder to a mug, pour in the boiling water, stir and cover for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in roasted chana for crunch.
Season with salt for a savoury version or a little jaggery for sweet, and eat straight from the mug.
why_it_works: Needs only a kettle and a mug
Roasted chana adds protein and crunch without cooking
Very low cost

name: ZITLAS Besan Dhokla Bites
description: Steamed gram-flour dhokla made in an idli mould, giving the classic Gujarati texture without deep steamer equipment.
ingredients: Eno fruit salt / baking soda — 3 g
instructions: Whisk besan, curd and water into a smooth, thick-pourable batter.
Just before steaming, mix in the fruit salt/baking soda — it will froth slightly.
Pour into a greased idli mould or shallow tin and steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 12-15 minutes.
Cool slightly, cut into squares.
Temper oil with mustard and sesame seeds and pour over the top.
why_it_works: Steamed, not fried — very low added fat
Uses standard home pressure cooker as a steamer
Good fiber from besan

name: ZITLAS No-Cook Sprouted Moong Chaat
description: A tangy, crunchy sprouted moong salad with onion, tomato and lemon — ready in five minutes with no heat at all.
instructions: Rinse the sprouts well.
Toss sprouts with onion, tomato and coriander in a bowl.
Add lemon juice and chaat masala.
Mix well and eat immediately for maximum crunch.
why_it_works: Zero cooking, zero cleanup beyond one bowl
High fiber and protein together
Very low calorie for weight-loss mornings

name: ZITLAS Bajra Khichdi Bowl
description: A pressure-cooker millet-and-moong khichdi that makes a warm, fibre-rich family breakfast bowl, especially suited to cooler mornings.
instructions: Rinse moong dal; combine with bajra flour, vegetables, turmeric and enough water in the cooker.
Pressure cook for 3-4 whistles until soft and porridge-like.
Once pressure releases, mash lightly for a smoother texture.
Temper ghee with cumin seeds and pour over the top before serving.
why_it_works: High-fibre millet base is unusual outside dinner khichdi
Good for cold mornings and shared family portions
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS Curd Rice with Roasted Peanuts
description: A cooling South Indian-style curd rice tempered with mustard, curry leaves and roasted peanuts — light, quick, and needs almost no active cooking.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chilli — 3 g
instructions: Mash the cold rice slightly and mix with curd and a splash of milk to loosen it.
In a small kadai, heat oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chilli and peanuts; roast until peanuts are golden.
Pour the tempering over the curd rice and mix.
Serve at room temperature or lightly chilled.
why_it_works: Very light on the stomach for hot mornings
Minimal cooking, mostly assembly
Good gut-friendly probiotic base

name: ZITLAS Soya Keema Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha where the filling is spiced, finely crumbled soya granules instead of meat keema — a vegetarian high-protein take on a keema paratha.
instructions: Saute onion, tomato, ginger-garlic paste and garam masala with soya granules until dry and well spiced; cool slightly.
Knead atta into a dough; roll a portion, place the soya filling in the centre, fold and seal.
Roll out gently into a thick paratha.
Roast on a tawa with a little oil on both sides until golden with brown spots.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Soya keema has more protein per gram than most meat keema
Filling doubles as a standalone snack too
Satisfying, higher-effort weekend breakfast

name: ZITLAS Peanut Banana Oats Smoothie Bowl
description: A thick, spoonable oats-and-banana smoothie topped with peanuts — a cold breakfast bowl for hot mornings, made entirely in a mixer.
instructions: Blend oats, banana, milk and curd together until thick and smooth.
Pour into a bowl — it should be thick enough to eat with a spoon, not sip.
Top with crushed peanuts and a few banana slices.
Eat immediately for best texture.
why_it_works: No heat needed, good for summer mornings
Banana adds natural sweetness without added sugar
Peanuts add crunch and healthy fat

name: ZITLAS Egg White Veggie Wrap
description: A lean egg-white omelette loaded with vegetables and rolled into a whole wheat wrap — designed for lower fat intake while keeping protein high.
instructions: Roll the atta into a thin roti and dry-roast it lightly; set aside.
Whisk egg whites with black pepper.
Heat oil in a pan, saute capsicum and onion for 2 minutes, then pour in egg whites and cook until just set, not rubbery.
Place the egg-white filling onto the roti and roll tightly.
Slice and serve.
why_it_works: Very low fat, high protein combination
Vegetables add volume and fiber without many calories
Good for a lean cutting phase

name: ZITLAS Rajma Paratha (Leftover Rescue)
description: Leftover cooked rajma is mashed and spiced to become a paratha stuffing, turning last night's dinner curry into a fresh breakfast.
instructions: Drain excess gravy from the leftover rajma and mash the beans coarsely with onion, ajwain and chilli powder.
Knead the atta into a dough; stuff a portion with the rajma mixture and seal.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve with curd or pickle.
why_it_works: Directly repurposes last night's leftovers instead of discarding them
Rajma brings both protein and fiber
No separate filling has to be cooked from scratch

name: ZITLAS Ragi Dosa with Tomato Chutney
description: A fibre-forward finger-millet dosa batter pan-cooked thin and crisp, served with a quick tomato chutney — a fiber-focused twist on a South Indian classic.
instructions: Whisk ragi flour, rice flour and curd with water into a thin, pourable batter; rest 15 minutes.
For chutney, blend tomato with green chilli and a pinch of salt, then temper with cumin seeds in a little oil.
Heat a tawa, pour batter in a circular motion from the edge inward to form a thin dosa.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until crisp; flip briefly.
Serve hot with the tomato chutney.
why_it_works: Ragi has notably more fiber and calcium than a plain rice dosa
No fermentation wait required
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS Sattu Paratha
description: A Bihar-style stuffed paratha filled with a spiced sattu mixture — a budget protein breakfast that also travels well for lunch.
instructions: Mix sattu with chopped onion, ajwain, pickle masala and a little water into a thick, moist stuffing.
Knead the atta into a dough, stuff with the sattu mixture and seal well.
Roll out carefully and roast on a tawa with mustard oil until well browned on both sides.
Serve hot with curd or pickle.
why_it_works: Sattu is one of the cheapest high-protein ingredients available in India
Filling stays moist without any dairy needed
Travels well for lunchboxes too

name: ZITLAS Makhana Yogurt Parfait
description: Layered Greek yogurt and roasted fox nuts (makhana) with a touch of honey — a light, crunchy breakfast that eats almost like a dessert.
instructions: Spoon a layer of Greek yogurt into a glass.
Sprinkle a layer of crushed roasted makhana over it.
Repeat the layers once more.
Drizzle honey on top just before serving to keep the makhana crunchy.
why_it_works: High protein-to-calorie ratio from Greek yogurt
Makhana adds crunch with very little fat
Zero cooking involved

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Dalia Upma
description: Broken wheat cooked upma-style with vegetables in a pressure cooker — a fibre-dense, family-portioned alternative to rava upma.
instructions: Dry-roast the dalia lightly until aromatic; set aside.
Heat oil in the cooker, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then saute onion and vegetables for 3-4 minutes.
Add the roasted dalia and water in a 1:2.5 ratio, season with salt.
Pressure cook for 2 whistles, then let pressure release naturally before opening.
why_it_works: Notably higher fiber than a rava-based upma
Cooks unattended in a pressure cooker
Large batch suits a family breakfast

name: ZITLAS Boiled Egg Sprouts Bowl
description: A no-cook combination of boiled eggs and mixed sprouts tossed with lemon and pepper — a fast, high-protein bowl for right after a morning workout.
instructions: Chop the boiled eggs into quarters.
Toss with sprouts and onion in a bowl.
Add lemon juice and black pepper.
Mix gently and eat immediately after your workout.
why_it_works: Fast-digesting protein combination suited for post-workout timing
Requires only a boiled egg made ahead — no stove needed at breakfast time
High protein for the calorie cost

name: ZITLAS Besan Savoury Toast
description: Whole wheat bread dipped in a spiced besan batter and pan-toasted, like a savoury French toast — a five-minute upgrade on plain toast.
instructions: Whisk besan with water, onion, turmeric and ajwain into a thick, spreadable batter.
Dip each bread slice into the batter, coating both sides.
Pan-toast on a lightly oiled tawa until golden on both sides.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Adds meaningful protein and fiber to an otherwise low-protein breakfast staple
Only one pan and five minutes of cooking
Cheaper than most spreads or jams

name: ZITLAS Thecha Peanut Sandwich
description: A Maharashtrian-style spicy peanut-garlic thecha spread inside a grilled whole wheat sandwich — a quick, bold-flavoured budget breakfast.
instructions: Dry-roast peanuts, then pound or blend coarsely with garlic and green chilli into a thick thecha paste.
Spread the thecha between two bread slices.
Grill on a lightly oiled tawa until both sides are golden and crisp.
Cut and serve hot.
why_it_works: Peanut base gives more protein and healthy fat than butter or jam
Very budget-friendly, no dairy required
Distinct regional flavour instead of a generic sandwich

name: ZITLAS Protein-Boosted Idli Sambar
description: Regular idli batter enriched with extra soaked urad and moong dal before steaming, served with a protein-added sambar using extra toor dal.
ingredients: Extra moong dal, soaked and blended in — 30 g
instructions: Blend the extra soaked moong dal into the fermented idli batter just before steaming, mixing gently to keep it airy.
Steam the batter in idli moulds for 10-12 minutes until a knife comes out clean.
Separately pressure cook toor dal with vegetables until soft, then simmer with sambar powder and tamarind to make the sambar.
Serve idlis hot with the sambar.
why_it_works: Extra dal in the batter raises protein without changing the familiar taste
Sambar itself becomes a second protein source, not just a side
Steamed, not fried

name: ZITLAS Paneer Roti Roll (Lunchbox)
description: Leftover roti spread with a mashed spiced paneer filling and rolled up — designed specifically to be packed and eaten a few hours later.
instructions: Warm the leftover roti lightly on a tawa so it stays pliable.
Mash paneer with onion, chaat masala and a little oil into a coarse filling.
Spread the filling along the roti and roll tightly.
Wrap in foil — it holds together well for 3-4 hours without going soggy.
why_it_works: Repurposes leftover roti instead of making fresh dough
Stays intact for a mid-morning lunchbox eat
Higher protein than a typical roti roll

name: ZITLAS Soya Brown Rice Prep Bowl
description: A make-ahead bowl of spiced soya chunks over brown rice, portioned into containers for grab-and-go mornings across the week.
instructions: Cook brown rice separately and let it cool fully before portioning (this keeps it from going mushy in storage).
Heat oil, saute onion and ginger-garlic paste, add vegetables and cook 4-5 minutes.
Add rehydrated soya chunks and garam masala, cook until well coated and slightly dry, about 8-10 minutes.
Divide brown rice and the soya mixture into 4 containers.
Refrigerate; reheat one portion each morning for up to 4 days.
why_it_works: One cooking session covers 4 mornings
Soya chunks are one of the highest-protein-per-rupee options available
Brown rice adds fiber compared to white rice

name: ZITLAS Peanut Sprouts Kanda Poha
description: Classic Maharashtrian kanda poha with peanuts, upgraded by folding in moong sprouts at the end for extra crunch and protein.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Rinse poha in a sieve under running water until softened; do not soak.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then add peanuts and roast lightly.
Add onion and saute until translucent.
Add turmeric and the rinsed poha, mix gently on low heat for 2-3 minutes.
Fold in the moong sprouts at the very end so they stay crunchy, and serve immediately.
why_it_works: Sprouts added at the end keep their crunch and boost protein over standard poha
Still recognisably the familiar dish, just meaningfully upgraded
Very quick and low cost

name: ZITLAS Egg Akuri on Toast
description: A Parsi-style softly spiced scrambled egg with ginger, chilli and coriander, served over toasted whole wheat bread.
instructions: Toast the bread slices until lightly crisp.
Heat oil, saute onion, ginger and green chilli until soft, then add tomato and cook until pulpy.
Beat the eggs and pour in; stir continuously on low heat for a soft, slightly wet scramble rather than dry.
Finish with chopped coriander and spoon over the toast.
why_it_works: Slow, low-heat scrambling keeps the egg tender rather than rubbery
A distinct regional variation on the usual bhurji
Balanced protein-to-carb ratio with the toast

name: ZITLAS Oats Idli
description: Ground rolled oats combined with urad dal batter and steamed like a regular idli — a fibre-forward variation for people who don't enjoy oats as porridge.
instructions: Grind rolled oats to a coarse flour and mix with the fermented urad dal batter and curd.
Rest the mixed batter for 10 minutes.
Add eno fruit salt just before steaming and mix gently.
Pour into greased idli moulds and steam for 10-12 minutes in a pressure cooker without the whistle.
why_it_works: Delivers oats' fiber benefit in a texture many people prefer over porridge
Steamed preparation stays low in added fat
Works well for people who dislike oats' usual mushy texture

name: ZITLAS Air-Fried Moong Dahi Vada
description: Mini moong dal vadas air-fried instead of deep-fried, soaked briefly in curd — a protein-forward, lower-oil take on dahi vada for breakfast.
instructions: Grind the soaked moong dal with ginger and green chilli into a thick batter; do not add water.
Shape into small discs and brush lightly with oil.
Air fry at 180°C for 12-15 minutes, flipping once, until golden.
Soak the air-fried vadas in whisked curd for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle roasted cumin powder and serve.
why_it_works: Air frying cuts most of the oil a normal fried vada would use
Moong dal delivers more protein than the usual urad-based vada
Curd adds a second protein layer

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Omelette Roll
description: A whole-egg omelette loaded with vegetables, rolled up like a wrap without any bread — a quick, low-carb office breakfast.
instructions: Beat the eggs with black pepper.
Heat oil in a flat pan, saute the vegetables for 2 minutes.
Pour the beaten egg evenly over the vegetables and cook on low-medium heat until just set.
Roll the omelette up from one side using a spatula.
Slice in half and serve.
why_it_works: No bread keeps carbs low while protein stays high
Cooked and rolled entirely in one pan
Ready in well under 15 minutes

name: ZITLAS Chana Dal Vegetable Cheela
description: A savoury chana dal batter crepe packed with grated vegetables — a fibre-and-protein alternative to a plain besan chilla.
ingredients: Chana dal, soaked and ground — 70 g
instructions: Grind the soaked chana dal with green chilli into a smooth, pourable batter.
Mix in the grated carrot and cabbage along with cumin seeds.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a thick cheela.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Chana dal has more fiber per gram than besan
Vegetables are mixed into the batter, not just a side garnish
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS No-Bake Peanut Chikki Bites
description: Small no-bake energy bites made from roasted peanuts and jaggery, portioned for a grab-and-go breakfast when there's genuinely no time to sit down.
instructions: Melt jaggery with ghee in a kadai on low heat until it forms a thick syrup.
Turn off the heat and quickly mix in the crushed peanuts, coating them evenly.
While still warm, shape into 8 small bite-sized balls.
Cool completely, then store in an airtight container for up to a week; grab 2 on your way out.
why_it_works: Genuinely eat-on-the-move — no bowl or spoon needed
Batch-made once, lasts most of a week
Uses jaggery instead of refined sugar

name: ZITLAS Bajra Roti with Peanut Chutney
description: A Rajasthani-style millet flatbread served with a dry roasted peanut chutney and a side of curd — a hearty, fibre-rich regional breakfast.
instructions: Knead bajra flour with warm water into a dough (it's less elastic than wheat, so pat it out by hand rather than rolling).
Cook the flattened roti on a hot tawa until browned on both sides, brushing with a little ghee.
For the chutney, dry-roast peanuts and pound coarsely with garlic, red chilli and salt.
Serve the roti hot with the peanut chutney and a bowl of curd on the side.
why_it_works: Bajra has more fiber and minerals than wheat
Peanut chutney adds protein without any dairy dependence
Traditional combination that's naturally balanced

name: ZITLAS Soya Milk Date Overnight Oats
description: A vegan overnight oats jar made with soya milk and chopped dates instead of honey — sweetened naturally and higher in plant protein.
instructions: Combine oats, soya milk, chopped dates and chia seeds in a jar.
Stir well so the chia doesn't clump.
Seal and refrigerate overnight.
Stir again before eating in the morning.
why_it_works: Fully vegan protein sources instead of dairy
Dates provide natural sweetness with fiber attached
Zero morning prep time

name: ZITLAS Lite Paneer Paratha
description: A stuffed paneer paratha made with a deliberately reduced-oil roasting method, keeping the classic flavour with meaningfully less added fat.
instructions: Mix paneer with onion, ajwain and garam masala; no oil needed in the filling itself.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the paneer mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a hot tawa using only a light brushing of oil rather than pooling oil, flipping to get even colour.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Uses a fraction of the oil a typical paratha uses while keeping the texture
Paneer keeps protein high even with less fat overall
Still recognisably the familiar comfort food

name: ZITLAS Soya Vermicelli Upma
description: Roasted vermicelli upma with soya granules folded in — a South Indian breakfast staple made noticeably more filling.
instructions: Dry-roast the vermicelli until light golden; set aside.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then saute onion and carrot for 3 minutes.
Add the rehydrated soya granules and cook 2 minutes.
Add the roasted vermicelli with hot water (roughly equal volume) and cook covered until the water is absorbed.
why_it_works: Soya granules meaningfully raise the protein of a usually low-protein dish
Still cooks in one pan in under 20 minutes
Familiar taste, upgraded composition

name: ZITLAS Chana Curd Bhel (No Cook)
description: Boiled chana tossed with curd, onion and tomato in a bhel-style mix — tangy, filling, and entirely no-cook.
instructions: Combine boiled chana, onion and tomato in a bowl.
Add curd and chaat masala, mix well.
Top with chopped coriander.
Eat immediately while the onion is still crisp.
why_it_works: Two protein sources combined with zero cooking
Curd makes it noticeably lighter than an oil-based chaat
Ready in under 10 minutes

name: ZITLAS Baked Egg Muffin Cups
description: Whisked eggs and chopped vegetables baked in a muffin tin into individual portions — a genuine meal-prep breakfast for the whole week.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C and lightly grease a 6-cavity muffin tin.
Whisk all the eggs together with salt and pepper.
Divide the chopped vegetables evenly among the muffin cups, then pour whisked egg over each.
Bake for 18-20 minutes until set and lightly domed.
Cool, then refrigerate; microwave one or two cups each morning for up to 4 days.
why_it_works: Six single-serve portions from one batch cooking session
Reheats in under a minute on busy mornings
Vegetables are baked in, not garnished after

name: ZITLAS Sabudana Peanut Khichdi
description: A protein-supported version of Maharashtrian sabudana khichdi, with a larger peanut ratio and a side of curd to balance out the starch-heavy sago base. Note: sabudana needs 4+ hours of prior soaking, not counted in active prep time below.
instructions: Soak sabudana in just enough water to cover it, for at least 4 hours or overnight, until pearls are soft but separate.
Heat oil, temper cumin seeds and green chilli, then saute diced potato until soft.
Add the soaked sabudana and crushed peanuts, tossing gently on low heat until translucent, about 6-8 minutes.
Serve hot with a side of curd for extra protein.
why_it_works: Deliberately peanut-heavy ratio compensates for sabudana's low protein
Curd on the side adds a second protein source
Traditional fasting-day dish made more nutritionally complete

name: ZITLAS Multigrain Uttapam
description: A thick, vegetable-topped pancake made from a multigrain batter (rice, urad and a portion of oats) — a heartier alternative to a plain dosa.
ingredients: Oats, ground and mixed in — 30 g
instructions: Mix ground oats into the fermented dosa batter and rest for 10 minutes.
Heat a tawa, pour a thick ladle of batter and spread only slightly (uttapam stays thick, unlike dosa).
Scatter onion and tomato over the top and press gently.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until the base is golden, then flip briefly.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Thicker format holds more toppings than a thin dosa
Oats addition adds fiber to a usually rice-heavy batter
Vegetables are cooked into the surface, not a side dish

name: ZITLAS Leftover Roti Chivda
description: Stale leftover rotis are torn into pieces and pan-toasted with peanuts and spices into a crunchy, chivda-style snack-breakfast — genuinely rescues rotis that would otherwise be thrown out.
ingredients: Leftover roti, torn into small pieces — 100 g
Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil in a kadai, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then roast the peanuts until golden.
Add onion and saute until soft.
Add the torn roti pieces and turmeric, tossing continuously on medium-high heat until the pieces crisp up slightly, about 5 minutes.
Serve hot as-is — it eats like a savoury chivda.
why_it_works: Rescues rotis heading for the bin rather than being reheated plain
Crisping the roti gives it a completely different texture from a reheated roti
Very low cost since the base ingredient is already leftover

name: ZITLAS One-Pan Hostel Paneer Chilla Wrap
description: A besan-paneer batter cooked directly as a folded wrap in a single pan — designed for a hostel room with just an induction plate and one pan.
instructions: Whisk besan with water, turmeric and chilli powder into a smooth batter.
Stir the crumbled paneer and onion directly into the batter.
Heat the single pan on the induction plate with a little oil, pour the batter in and spread into a thick round.
Cook 2-3 minutes until the base sets, flip, and cook the other side.
Fold in half like a wrap and eat straight from the pan.
why_it_works: Everything — batter, protein and cooking — happens in one pan
No separate filling step, unlike a stuffed paratha
Realistic for genuine one-induction-one-pan hostel setups

name: ZITLAS Portion-Controlled Moong Dal Halwa
description: A small, deliberately portion-capped serving of moong dal halwa made with less ghee than the traditional version — a controlled way to have a classic sweet at breakfast.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and coarsely ground — 40 g
instructions: Heat ghee in a kadai and roast the ground moong dal on low heat until it turns golden and aromatic, about 8 minutes.
Add milk gradually, stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Once thickened, add jaggery and cardamom powder, stirring until it melts in and the mixture pulls together.
Serve warm in a small bowl — this recipe is intentionally single-serving to keep the portion controlled.
why_it_works: Single-serving format prevents the usual over-serving of a rich halwa
Meaningfully less ghee than a restaurant-style halwa while staying satisfying
Moong dal itself adds real protein, unusual for a dessert

name: ZITLAS Egg Oats Savoury Porridge
description: An unusual but practical combination — oats cooked savoury in stock-like water, finished with a stirred-in egg for extra protein, like a simple congee.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until soft.
Add water and bring to a simmer, then stir in the oats and cook 4-5 minutes until porridge-like.
Beat the egg lightly and stir it into the simmering oats in a thin stream, so it cooks into ribbons rather than clumping.
Season with black pepper and a dash of soy sauce, and serve hot.
why_it_works: Savoury porridge format is a genuinely different way to eat oats, not just sweetened oats again
Egg stirred in raises protein meaningfully over plain oats
One pan, under 15 minutes

name: ZITLAS Rajma Oats Tikki Sandwich
description: Leftover rajma mashed with oats as a binder, shaped into tikkis and pan-fried, then sandwiched between toasted bread — a leftover-rescue recipe with a sandwich format.
instructions: Drain excess liquid from the leftover rajma and mash it coarsely.
Mix in ground oats, onion and chilli powder — the oats bind the mixture and add fiber.
Shape into a flat tikki and pan-fry in oil until crisp on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Toast the bread lightly and sandwich the tikki inside with a spread of your choice.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Oats replace refined breadcrumbs as the binder, adding fiber instead of empty carbs
Second genuinely different way to use leftover rajma beyond the paratha version
Familiar sandwich format for people who want something handheld

name: ZITLAS Chaas and Roasted Chana Combo
description: A savoury spiced buttermilk paired with a small side of roasted chana — a light drink-plus-snack combo breakfast for very hot mornings or a light-appetite day.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 3 g
instructions: Whisk the buttermilk with roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Pour into a glass.
Serve alongside a small bowl of roasted chana to eat on the side.
No cooking or cleanup beyond one glass and one bowl.
why_it_works: Very light option for mornings with a poor appetite or hot weather
Two small protein sources instead of one large meal
Genuinely no-cook and near-zero cleanup

name: ZITLAS Foxtail Millet Upma
description: Foxtail millet cooked upma-style with vegetables and peanuts — a premium-grain alternative to rava upma with a lower glycemic profile.
instructions: Rinse the foxtail millet well and soak for 10 minutes.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, roast the peanuts, then add vegetables and saute 3 minutes.
Add the soaked millet and water in a 1:2 ratio, cover and simmer for 10-12 minutes until soft.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.
why_it_works: Lower glycemic index than rava, useful for steadier morning energy
Naturally gluten-free grain option
Still cooks in one pan like a familiar upma

name: ZITLAS Paneer Bhurji Multigrain Bowl
description: Spiced scrambled paneer served over a base of mixed millets instead of bread or rice — a bowl format for people who prefer eating with a spoon.
instructions: Cook the foxtail millet ahead (or use leftover cooked millet) and keep warm.
Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add turmeric and chilli powder.
Add crumbled paneer and cook 3-4 minutes, stirring gently so it stays soft, not rubbery.
Spoon the paneer bhurji over the millet base in a bowl and serve.
why_it_works: Millet base gives more fiber than the usual bread pairing with bhurji
Bowl format suits people who find paratha or toast too heavy
High protein-to-carb ratio

name: ZITLAS Tofu Bhurji Toast
description: Crumbled tofu scrambled with Indian spices, served over toast — a fully vegan alternative to egg bhurji with a similar texture.
instructions: Toast the bread slices lightly.
Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, then add turmeric and chilli powder.
Add crumbled tofu and cook 4-5 minutes, mashing slightly for an egg-bhurji-like texture.
Spoon the tofu bhurji over the toast and serve.
why_it_works: Vegan option with a texture close enough to egg bhurji to satisfy the same craving
Tofu absorbs Indian spices well despite being a non-traditional ingredient here
Quick, one-pan filling

name: ZITLAS Quinoa Vegetable Poha-Style Bowl
description: Cooked quinoa tempered and tossed poha-style with peanuts and vegetables — for users who want a complete-protein grain instead of flattened rice.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Cook quinoa ahead of time (or use leftover cooked quinoa) and keep aside.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, roast peanuts, then saute onion and carrot for 3 minutes.
Add turmeric and the cooked quinoa, tossing gently for 3-4 minutes until heated through.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Quinoa is a rare complete-protein plant grain, unlike rice or poha
Same familiar tempering technique as regular poha, so it's easy to adapt to
Good general-fitness option though a pricier grain

name: ZITLAS Curd Sattu Cooler Bowl
description: A cold, spoonable no-cook bowl combining sattu with thick curd instead of water — heavier and more filling than the Sattu Power Shot drink, meant for a sit-down breakfast rather than a grab-and-go one.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 3 g
instructions: Whisk sattu into the curd until fully smooth, with no dry lumps.
Fold in finely chopped onion.
Season with roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Top with coriander and eat with a spoon, straight from the bowl.
why_it_works: Bowl format makes it more filling than the drink version of sattu
Two protein sources — dal-based and dairy — in one no-cook dish
No equipment beyond a bowl and whisk
